_doc: Human verdicts on cells where the printed page disagrees with the catalog.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `apply_survey.py --conflicts` regenerates the queue from the sidecars
every run, so without a decision record it reprints the same items forever and nobody can
tell 'not yet reviewed' from 'reviewed, catalog was right'. The queue is derived; the verdict
is not. This is the verdict. `results/ditto_review_*.tsv` has the same missing half --
PIPELINE.md #1 asks to 'record which volume it was decided for' and nothing ever did.
VERDICTS
book-wins     the page is right and the CSV is wrong. THE ONLY verdict that overwrites a
non-empty cell, and it needs a reason naming the evidence.
catalog-wins  the CSV is right and the read is wrong. Retires the conflict.
both-right    both are true of different things -- a compiler vs the house that published.
Retires the conflict and marks the row as wanting a field split.
needs-image   text cannot settle it; hand to phase 3. Retires it from THIS queue only.
wontfix       not worth resolving; say why.
A decision is keyed (source, id, column) and is matched only against a conflict. It cannot
invent a cell, and a `book-wins` on a cell that no longer conflicts is a no-op.
Seeded only with verdicts docs/SURVEY_PLAN.md ALREADY establishes. The open calls -- the
9-row `spooner` cluster, and the 9 year reads that grabbed boilerplate or listing text --
are deliberately left undecided: the spooner cluster needs a human, and recording
`catalog-wins` on the year reads would paper over an extractor bug that should be fixed at
the source instead.

decisions.reason: Smith is the compiler the title is named for (SMITH'S BROOKLYN DIRECTORY); Charles Jenkins is the house that published it, per the copyright line on leaf 28. SURVEY_PLAN.md: these want separate `compiler` / `publisher` / `printer` fields.
Same Smith/Jenkins split as 1857BPL, attested by the target card on leaf 1 ('Published by Charles Jenkins').

Read is OCR-damaged ('GEORGE TTBiNfiTriM' for Upington). SURVEY_PLAN.md is explicit that character-level damage must stay a conflict rather than be matched loosely -- anything loose enough to match this would match unrelated houses.
OCR-damaged read ('GEORGE UHNUTON' for Upington); same rule as 1908BPL.
OCR-damaged read ('D. L0NGW0RTH' -- zeros for O's, which defeats the letters-only containment pass on purpose).
